title: Unsupervised Heterogeneous Graph Rewriting Attack via Node Clustering

problem.claim: Heterogeneous graph pre-training models require robustness verification, while existing supervised graph attacks are limited to settings with available labels.

gap.claim: Unsupervised attacks for verifying the robustness of heterogeneous graph pre-training remain insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: HGAC is an unsupervised heterogeneous graph rewriting attack that attacks heterogeneous graph pre-training models without using labels.
The method combines heterogeneous edge rewriting, a heterogeneous graph contrastive learning surrogate model, and node-clustering pseudo-labels to guide structural attack optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe HGAC as a novel unsupervised heterogeneous graph rewriting attack via node clustering.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report powerful HGAC attack performance across node classification, node clustering, metapath prediction, and visualization tasks under poisoning and evasion attacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Self-supervised learning has become successful in graph learning, including heterogeneous graph pre-training.
Robustness verification for heterogeneous graph pre-training is a research gap, and supervised attacks do not address label-unavailable scenarios.
HGAC performs unsupervised heterogeneous graph rewriting using edge rewriting, an HGCL surrogate, and node-clustering pseudo-labels.
The authors report strong attack performance across multiple downstream tasks and both poisoning and evasion settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not detail the edge-rewriting constraints or how rationality and concealment are measured.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported attack performance.
